quote: Because Schedule 4.4 is empty, the closing condition in SPA § 7.2(c) (receipt of all consents listed on Schedule 4.4) is technically satisfied without any consent actually being obtained. The buyer could close and *then* discover that Vantrell has the right to terminate.
reason: The memo quotes Supply Agreement § 14.2 in full. That includes the >50% voting stock change being deemed an assignment, the requirement for Supplier's prior written consent, and the 30-day termination right. The memo applies this to the 100% stock sale. It explains that SPA § 4.4 and Disclosure Schedule 4.4 ('None') fail to disclose the consent and that the § 7.2(c) closing condition does not cover it. It also notes the capped indemnity recourse and recommends making the consent a closing condition and correcting the schedule.
